To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the LP concept is applicable in Lisbon and (2) it is possible to extrapolate freight trip generation per delivery characteristics from a small sample of establishments to the entire population of establishments within a city, with an acceptable level of accuracy.

“The Logistic Profiles concept is a promising tool for urban freight analysis and policy development, but it needs to be further developed and tested, and its use must be adapted to local conditions”.

(a) freight trips can be extrapolated from a small sample of establishments; (b) freight delivery characteristics can be attributed to a sample of establishments, using a probabilistic model; (c) the LP concept can be used to identify homogeneous urban zones, in the context of urban logistics, and (d) the LP concept is transferable, but its application is subject to local particularities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the concept of Logistic Profiles (LP) in the analysis of urban logistics in a city.
the application of the LP concept in a case study and the testing of the concept itself, in order to assess its potential for use as a tool for freight movement analysis and policy.
the development of the Logistics Profile (Macario 2013) concept and its potential for use in the field of urban logistics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LPs can be useful to analyze urban freight movement policy, but further research is needed to confirm the hypothesis and the proposed methodology.
LPs have been proven as a potential tool to ease the transfer of best practices in urban freight transport and logistics.
the LP concept is a promising approach for urban logistics analysis, which could be further explored and tested in other cities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methodology has shown to be useful to test LPs and that some LPs have been identified in a real case study, which can be used to ease the transfer of urban freight policies.
the LP concept can be used as a departure to analyze urban logistics in cities, and to ease the transfer of best practices between cities.
we have shown that LPs can be used to identify groups of zones with similar freight generation and delivery profiles.

, when applied to the case study, the LP concept was able to identify groups of urban zones that share similarities in terms of the social and built environments and delivery characteristics.
